title: Shell-like quoted tokenizer
instructions:
Implement `ShellTokenizer(text: str)` in `shell_tokens.py` and its `tokens() -> list[str]` method.
Each call to `tokens()` parses the entire original text afresh, returning a new list. The other
starter methods are implementation helpers and may be changed.
Rules:
- Outside quotes, only space, tab, carriage return, and newline separate tokens. Repeated
  separators are ignored; empty or whitespace-only input returns `[]`.
- Single or double quotes begin a quoted fragment; matching quotes end it and are removed.
  Quoted fragments and unquoted text with no separator concatenate into one token.
  Even an empty quoted fragment creates a token.
- Inside single quotes every character except the closing single quote is literal, including
  backslashes and double quotes.
- Outside quotes and inside double quotes, backslash consumes the next character and appends
  it literally, even whitespace, a quote, another backslash, or a newline.
- An unmatched quote or a backslash without a following character (outside single quotes)
  raises `ValueError`. No partial result is returned.
- `#`, `$`, and shell operators are ordinary characters. There are no comments or expansions.

## Files
- `shell_tokens.py`
